key_insight: The paper shows that the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization cannot be closed under common similarity assumptions, and only a stronger combination of assumptions yields a better time complexity bound.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this means heterogeneous worker data can impose unavoidable latency and convergence penalties unless stronger structural conditions are known to hold.
method: Proves impossibility results for randomized algorithms under first- and second-order similarity assumptions.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still cannot remove the gap.
Derives a new bound using strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and complexity bounds rather than empirical experiments or benchmark data.
watch_item: The improved guarantee depends on relatively strong assumptions, so it may not transfer to real systems where worker data distributions are only loosely structured.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
